text: Checked my phone eleven times during dinner. Nothing from the hospital. Pushed the food around and went to bed at nine.
Didn't take my coat off for an hour after I got in. Just sat on the stairs with it on.
I've reorganised the cupboard under the sink twice today. The results come out tomorrow.
Still setting two cups out in the morning. Caught myself again today and put one back.
Hummed in the shower. Didn't notice till halfway through the second song.
Closed the laptop at three, opened it, closed it, opened it. Read the same paragraph of the complaint nine times. Went for a walk and walked fast.
Everyone else left the party at midnight and I stayed to help clear up so I wouldn't have to go back to the flat yet.
Turned the radio off halfway home and drove the rest in silence with the window down. Didn't need anything.
Kept the receipt from the café where Farah said it. It's in the drawer with the other things I don't look at.
Took the stairs two at a time to tell Dev. Forgot my keys in the door. He laughed at me and I didn't care.
Read the email from Marco four times and then went and cleaned the oven, which has needed doing since March.
Put the certificate on the fridge. Then moved it to the hall. Then back to the fridge where Mum will see it on Sunday.
Three alarms set for tomorrow. Clothes on the chair. Shoes by the door. Lying here doing the route in my head.
The leftovers are still in the fridge from Tuesday. I keep meaning to. I keep meaning to do a lot of things.
I watered the plants, all of them, even the one on the top shelf. First time in weeks they've all had a drink.
Deleted the draft message to Priya for the sixth time. Put the phone in the other room. Got it back.
Scrolled past the photos from the trip without stopping. Then scrolled back up. Then put the phone face down.
Said 'fine' when Jonas asked how the meeting went, and then went out to the garage and sorted the screws by size for an hour.
Bought the good bread and the good butter and sat in the window seat with the paper. Nobody rang. Didn't want them to.
Didn't correct Aunt Bea when she called me by my sister's name. Fourth time this visit. Washed up very slowly.
Texted everyone the photo of the sign with my name on it. Then texted it again to the family chat in case they'd missed it.
Left the group chat on mute. Watched the number of unread go up from across the room and didn't go over.
Wrote the list, then wrote a list of the lists. Then sat looking at the pen.
Slammed the cupboard. Apologised to the cupboard. Slammed it again, quieter.
Walked the long way past Hana's old flat. Light was on. Somebody else's curtains.
Fell asleep with the lamp on and the book open on my chest. Woke at two, turned the page, kept reading.
Rang Mum back straight away. Didn't let it ring out like usual. Kept her on the line twenty minutes about nothing.
Bit my nails for the first time since school. Noticed when I saw the blood.
Didn't put the music on in the car. Didn't put the news on. Drove home with just the engine.
Checked the tracking page for the ring eleven times before lunch. It's in Coventry. Coventry!
Took a different route so I wouldn't pass the office. Added twenty minutes. Worth it.
Ate standing up at the counter again. The table has the post on it. The post has been on it for nine days.
Sat in the car park for ten minutes after the appointment. Then drove to the garden centre for no reason and bought bulbs.
Hugged Samir a second longer than usual at the door. He noticed. Neither of us said anything.
Ironed everything in the basket, including the tea towels. The call's at nine.
Laughed out loud on the bus at the message from Kemi. The woman opposite looked. Laughed again.
Reread the rejection, then opened the spreadsheet of the other forty-one. Added a row. Closed it.
Didn't sit in Dad's chair. Nobody has. It's been six months and we all walk round it.
Took the dog out twice, cleaned the bathroom, rang my sister. Anything but open that envelope.
Put the kettle on, forgot about it, put it on again. Third time I drank it.
Signed the card from everyone and wrote three lines where everyone else wrote one. Then crossed one out.
Walked past the mirror in the hall and stopped and looked, properly, for the first time in a while. Nodded at myself.
Every time the door went downstairs I looked up. It's a shared building. It was never going to be him.
Yes to the extra shift. Yes to the school thing. Yes to Mum's hospital run. Said yes with my eyes closed.
Left the washing on the line overnight. Left the dishes. Left the phone on silent. Watched the whole film.
Typed the reply to Greg in capitals, deleted it, typed it in lower case, deleted it, sent 'Noted.'
Counted the sleeps out loud to Zoe at bedtime and she corrected me. It's four, not five. She's right. Four.
Made Grandad's recipe for the first time since. Got the cinnamon wrong. Ate it anyway, slowly, at his end of the table.
Stood at the back door for ages after the call from the school, not going in, not going out.
Said 'that's fine' to Rosa in a voice that wasn't fine and then went and hoovered the stairs very thoroughly.
Put the old photo of us back on the shelf. It's been in the drawer since spring.
Stopped to watch the heron for ten minutes on the way to work. Was late. Didn't mind being late.
Sat in the meeting with my nails in my palm. Smiled when Caroline finished. Went to the toilets and ran the tap.
Dinner for one at the table with a candle, like the book said. Blew it out after ten minutes and ate in front of the telly.
Answered the phone on the first ring all day. Jumped when the doorbell went. It was the parcel.
Walked out of the exam and didn't check the answers with anyone. Went straight for a bun. Ate it on the wall in the sun.
Three browser tabs of flats in Lisbon open. Closed them. Opened them. Screenshotted one.
Found myself telling the barista about Nico's results. The barista. She was very nice about it.
Didn't go to the thing. Said I had a cold. Sat in the dark with the telly off listening to the neighbours have people round.
Left work at five on the dot and didn't look back at the building. Didn't take the laptop. Walked home the long way.
Woke up before the alarm and lay there with my hand on Idris's back, listening to the rain. Didn't move for an hour.
Started the car, turned it off, went back in and hugged the kids again. Then drove to the hospital.
Brushed my teeth sitting on the edge of the bath. Toothpaste on the floor. Left it.
Kept the voicemail from Dad. Listen to it on the way to work sometimes. Twenty-two seconds about a lawnmower.
Tidied my desk, watered the office plant, made Ana a tea without being asked. Hummed. Ana asked what was wrong with me.
Clenched my jaw so hard through the call that it still aches. Took the dog round the block three times after.
Looked at the list on the fridge and took one thing off it. Just one. Then made a cup of tea and sat down.
Took the long road through the hills home from the funeral. Pulled over at the top. Sat there till the light went.
Put the running shoes by the door last night. Ran this morning. Put them by the door again.
Checked on Mia four times in the night even though she's fine, she's completely fine, the doctor said so.
Got to the end of the day and realised I hadn't looked at my phone since lunch. Found it in the garden. In the shed. Fine.
Put the extra chair back in the cupboard before anyone came. Nobody asked who it was for.
Said thank you to the bus driver like I meant it. Held the door for three people. Tipped double at lunch.
Didn't go upstairs when I heard Jem crying. Stood at the bottom with my hand on the rail, counting to twenty. Went up at twenty.
Wore the shirt I've been saving. No reason. Nowhere to go. Just wanted to see it on.
Walked past the pub where we used to go. Didn't go in. Didn't cross the road to avoid it either. Progress, I suppose.
Put Kwame's drawing in a frame. An actual frame, from a shop. It's a dog, apparently.
Set the table for one properly, cloth and everything, then ate on the sofa with the plate on my knees.
Cancelled the dentist, the dinner, and the call with Ines. Told them all I'd rebook. Lay down on the floor of the living room.
Wrote his name on the fogged-up window and then wiped it off before Lotte came in.
